subject: ent
title: Tracheostomy and Airway Foreign Bodies

steps.tx: **Tracheostomy indications** group into upper airway obstruction bypass, prolonged ventilation access, pulmonary toilet in weak cough and protection during major head and neck surgery. Emergency obstruction from tumour, infection or bilateral palsy heads the list, while intensive care weaning dominates elective practice numerically. Every indication is an airway decision first, because the tube treats access and protection rather than the underlying disease itself.
steps.say: Obstruction bypass, ventilation access and secretion clearance give the main tracheostomy indications. Head and neck surgery protection adds a planned surgical group. The tube provides access rather than disease treatment.

vis.alt: Tracheobronchial anatomy diagram with airway foreign body locations in the bronchial tree.
vis.caption: Tracheobronchial anatomy and foreign body sites. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Tracheostomy complications** divide into immediate bleeding and false passage, early tube displacement or blockage and late tracheal stenosis, fistula and scar problems. Displaced tubes in the first days are lethal because the tract is immature, so stay sutures, spare tubes and bedside algorithms guard every new tracheostomy. Blockage by secretions is prevented by humidification and suction discipline rather than rescued repeatedly by emergency changes.
steps.say: Bleeding, displacement, blockage and late stenosis divide complications by timing. Immature tracts make early displacement lethal without bedside safeguards. Humidification and suction prevent blockage better than rescue.

steps.tx: **Cricothyroidotomy** is the emergency front of neck access through the cricothyroid membrane when intubation and oxygenation both fail, faster and more superficial than formal tracheostomy. It is a rescue bridge, converted to formal tracheostomy later, and is relatively contraindicated in young children whose cricoid is narrowest. Cannot intubate cannot oxygenate drills rehearse this sequence until it is automatic under stress.
steps.say: Membrane puncture access rescues failed intubation with failed oxygenation emergencies. Later conversion gives formal tracheostomy after stabilisation. Young children need caution because cricoid is narrowest.

steps.tx: **Tracheostomy tube types** vary by cuff, fenestration and material: cuffed tubes seal for ventilation, uncuffed tubes suit children and weaning, fenestrated tubes allow speech with the outer cannula system, and metallic tubes serve long term care without cuffs. Inner cannulas remove for cleaning and are the first check in any blocked tube alarm. Speaking valves restore voice in suitable cuff deflated patients during rehabilitation.
steps.say: Cuff, fenestration and material variations suit ventilation, weaning and speech needs respectively. Inner cannula removal is first in blocked tube assessment. Speaking valves restore voice during rehabilitation suitably.

steps.tx: **Rigid bronchoscopy** is the instrument for airway foreign bodies because it ventilates through its barrel while grasping forceps remove objects under vision. Flexible scopes inspect and assist but cannot extract large objects safely through their channels. Theatre setup includes multiple forceps types, optical graspers and tracheostomy standby, because object loss at the glottis converts partial obstruction into complete obstruction instantly.
steps.say: Ventilating rigid scopes remove foreign bodies under vision with grasping forceps. Flexible scopes provide inspection without large extraction capability. Glottic loss converts partial obstruction completely and needs standby.

vis.alt: Diagram of foreign body aspiration sites in the tracheobronchial tree of a child.
vis.caption: Aspiration sites in the bronchial tree. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Foreign body bronchus** lodges most often in the right main bronchus because it is wider, shorter and more vertical than the left, continuing the tracheal line. Peanut fragments swell with airway secretions and fragment on grasping, needing piecemeal removal and re inspection. Delayed presentation mimics pneumonia or asthma for weeks, so unilateral wheeze or recurrent same site pneumonia earns bronchoscopy in children.
steps.say: Right bronchus anatomy receives most aspirated objects by width and vertical course. Peanut fragments swell and fragment during grasping attempts. Same site recurrent pneumonia needs bronchoscopy in children.

steps.tx: The **right main bronchus** rule pairs with peanut as the classic organic object in toddlers, whose oil irritates mucosa into chemical pneumonitis and granulation that bleeds at late removal. Inorganic objects tolerate delay better, but every suspected bronchial body is removed under controlled conditions rather than chased with blind suction or fogarty passes. Post removal bronchoscopy confirms clearance and samples infected secretions distally.
steps.say: Toddler peanut aspiration irritates mucosa with oil induced inflammation and granulation. Controlled removal replaces blind suction attempts in suspect cases. Repeat inspection confirms clearance after extraction.

steps.tx: **Intubation granuloma** forms on the vocal process after prolonged or traumatic intubation, producing hoarseness after extubation that mimics palsy until endoscopy shows the contact lesion. Voice rest and reflux control heal most, with excision for persistent masses after palsy is excluded by mobility assessment. Its posterior site links it to contact ulcer biology covered in benign lesions.
steps.say: Post intubation granuloma gives hoarseness and mimics palsy until endoscopy. Mobility assessment is needed to exclude nerve injury before lesion treatment. Voice rest with reflux control heals most lesions.

steps.tx: **Acquired subglottic stenosis** follows prolonged intubation or tracheostomy injury at the cricoid, presenting weeks later with biphasic stridor and failed extubation in intensive care graduates. Cotton Myer grading by tube size guides dilatation, laser, expansion grafting or resection choices, shared with congenital stenosis teaching. Prevention is cuff pressure discipline and timely tracheostomy decisions during prolonged ventilation.
steps.say: Cricoid injury after prolonged tubes gives biphasic stridor weeks later. Tube size grading guides dilatation to resection choices. Cuff discipline prevents stenosis during ventilation.

steps.tx: **Cotton-Myer grading** converts stenosis into a common language: grade one under fifty percent, grade two fifty to seventy, grade three seventy to ninety nine and grade four no lumen. Grades one and two often dilate or observe, grade three needs expansion surgery discussion and grade four needs resection based reconstruction. The same scale closes congenital and acquired lessons, examinations use it interchangeably.
steps.say: Percentage grades give stenosis a common language across causes. Lower grades dilate while higher grades need reconstruction surgery. Examinations apply the scale interchangeably by cause.

cards.b: Cricothyroidotomy through cricothyroid membrane in cannot intubate cannot oxygenate; convert to tracheostomy later.
Right main bronchus (wider, shorter, more vertical); peanut in toddlers fragments and needs rigid bronchoscopy.
One under 50 percent, two 50 to 70, three 70 to 99, four no lumen; higher grades need reconstruction.

keys: Early displaced tracheostomy is lethal without safeguards
Unilateral wheeze in a child is foreign body until disproved
